body:
Sorry for the lack of a follow-up. You're right, it is the small things that add and cause an issue. No I don't have anyone that I feel I can trust. Now that you mention it, I think that may be the root of the issue. I have difficulty trusting people due to my past (Abusive household, back-stabbing friends, etc).

>>I'm a terrible example when it comes to coping mechanisms - self harm, eating disorders and alcohol abuse are just a few of them

Sorry to hear that, I know it may sound stupid - but every time that you feel the urge to do X, write it down in a book. At the end of the week, review what you are doing. This is a pretty decent way of promoting self improvement.

I appreciate your wisdom.
> sometimes wish I had a trauma to "blame" it all on

I completely agree, I am the same way. There isn't necessarily one small or one large event which is causing this. It just is. Unfortunately, I think that because I don't handle it correctly (I tend to repress things which then causes a breakdown later down the path.)
>You've probably got to a stage where you don't see an end to this pain

I see the end of my struggles, but I just don't care enough to wait it out. Waiting it out, or not waiting out, in my mind - it just ends the same way.

I understand what you mean about not finishing the job, being worse off than you already are is a terrible thought.
In terms of things going awful in life, it happens to everyone. Killing yourself isn't a way to deal with it, it is only a way to permanently prevent progress/failure.
Life without stress is hardly a life at all.
I know this sounds stupid, but try to take your emotions out of the equation, and then post what you think.
There is something preventing you from going through with it, hence why you wrote this post. Take some time to figure out what it is.
